Rashi on Eruvin 24a:10:1.english: And then it was perforated again - Next to the seal.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:11:1.hebrew: ותיקנה - הוא הדין כי לא תיקנה נמי, עדיין טמא מדרס הוא. והא דנקט תיקנה — לרבותא, דאי לאו הכי, תו לא איצטריך למימר נפסקה השניה וכו':
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:11:1.english: And he repaired it - The same law applies even if he did not repair it as well; it is still impure with midras-impurity. And that which [the Mishnah] formulated, "and he repaired it," was for the sake of the novel ruling, for if it were not so, there would be no further need to say, "[If] the second broke," etc.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:12:1.hebrew: טהור מן המדרס - דתו לא הוה כלי, ולא חזי למדרס — מלטמא תו אדם וכלים:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:12:1.english: Pure from [the impurity of] treading - For it was no longer a vessel, and is not fit for treading — [so it is pure] from further defiling people and vessels.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:12:2.hebrew: אבל - כלי הוא, דחזי לתשמיש אחרינא, ועדיין טומאת מגע מדרס עליו — שהרי בשעת פרישתו מן האוזן, שעדיין הוא מדרס לקבל טומאה לטמא כלים, קיבל טומאה מאביו, והוי ראשון לטומאה, ומטמא אוכלין ומשקין:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:12:2.english: However - It is [still] a vessel, as it is fit for another use, and the impurity of contact with a midras is still upon it; for at the time of its separation from the ear, when it was still a midras with regard to contracting impurity to defile vessels, it received impurity from its “father” [the primary source of impurity], and [thus] it is a first-degree derivative of impurity, and it defiles food and drink.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:14:1.hebrew: פנים חדשות - אין אזנים הללו ממנו, ומשניתקנו לא דרסן הזב, ומטומאה הראשונה טיהרו — שהרי אין זה סנדל ראשון:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:14:1.english: A new entity - These ears are not from it, and since they were repaired, the zav did not tread upon them, and they became pure from the first impurity — for behold, this is not the original sandal.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:15:1.english: This is not a human being - Rather, [he is] an angel.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:15:2.english: One such as this is a human being - A great man.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:16:1.hebrew: רחבה שאחורי הבתים - ואין פתח הבית פתוח לה — הויא מוקפת שלא לדירה. ואי יותר מבית סאתים היה, אין מטלטלין בה אלא בארבע אמות:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:16:1.english: An open yard behind the houses - And [where] the entrance of the house does not open into it, it is [an area] enclosed not for residential purposes. And if it was larger than two beit se’ah, one may carry in it only within four cubits.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:17:1.english: And if one opened an entrance to it - From the house.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:18:1.hebrew: פשיטא - דבפתח ולבסוף הוקף שרי, שהרי הוקף לשם פתח:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:18:1.english: It is obvious - That where he opened [an entrance] and afterward it was enclosed, it is permitted, for it was enclosed for the sake of the entrance.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:18:2.english: It is necessary only where there is a threshing floor in it - [There was] a threshing floor behind the house prior to the enclosure of the yard.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:18:3.english: Lest you say he opened it with the threshing floor in mind - And not with the intention of enclosing an open area there.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:1:1.english: Is nullified relative to the greater part - And it is as though it were entirely sown.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:1:2.hebrew: והוה ליה קרפף יותר מבית סאתים - ואע"ג דהוקף לדירה, חשוב כלא הוקף לדירה — דהא הוי כולו גינה, ובגינה לא מהני הוקף לדירה:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:1:2.english: And it is a karpef greater than two beit se’a - Even though it was enclosed for dwelling purposes, it is considered as [though it were] not enclosed for dwelling purposes, for it is entirely a garden, and for a garden, [being] enclosed for dwelling purposes is of no avail.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:2:1.hebrew: דלא הוי - ההוא מיעוט דנזרע בית סאתים, דלא חשיב להבדל מן החצר ולהקרות לו שם לבדו:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:2:1.english: That it is not - That minority that was sown [is not] two beit se’ah, as it is not significant [enough] to be separated from the courtyard and designated with a name of its own.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:2:2.hebrew: אבל בית סאתים - נקרא קרפף שלא הוקף לדירה. ואע"ג דאילו הוה באנפי נפשיה כבית סאתים לא מיתסר, הכא, דנפרץ לחצר וחצר נפרצה לו, קיימא לן דאסור לטלטל מקרפף לחצר, דהוי רשות הנפרצה למקום האסור לה, ואוסרין הרשויות זו לזו, ואין מטלטלין לא בזה ולא בזה:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:2:2.english: However, [if it is] two beit se’a - It is considered a karpef that was not enclosed for dwelling. And even though if it were on its own [an area] of two beit se’a it would not be prohibited, here, where it is breached into the courtyard and the courtyard is breached into it, we maintain that it is prohibited to carry from a karpef to a courtyard, as it is a domain breached into an area forbidden to it, and the domains prohibit one another, and one may carry neither in this one nor in that one.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:3:1.english: According to whose [opinion] - Do we say that they are two [separate] domains?

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:3:2.hebrew: כרבנן - דפליגי עליה דר"'ש בפ' כל גגות (עירובין דף פט.), ואמרי: כל חד וחד רשות לעצמו. ואע"ג דליכא דיורין בהו דליסרו אהדדי — אין מטלטלין מזה לזה:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:3:2.english: According to the Rabbis - Who disagree with Rabbi Shimon in the chapter [entitled] Kol Gagot (Eruvin 89a), and say: Each and every one is a domain unto itself. And even though there are no residents in them to forbid [carrying] to one another — one may not carry from this [one] to that [one].

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:4:1.hebrew: לקולא - דאפילו המיעוט בית סאתים, דמיקרי קרפף — כיון דבאנפי נפשיה שרי, השתא נמי שרי, ולא אסרי אהדדי; דאילו היה מחיצה ביניהן, הוה שרי לטלטולי מזה לזה כר"'ש, והשתא דנפרצו זה לזה — לא נפרצו לרשות האסור לה. אבל יותר מבית סאתים נעשה כרמלית, ובהא אפילו ר"ש מודה דאין מטלטלין מחצר לקרפף יותר מבית סאתים שלא הוקף לדירה; והכא דנפרצו זה לזה, הרי כל אחד נפרץ למקום האסור לו:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:4:1.english: As a leniency - That even if the minority [sown area] is two beit se'a, which is called a karpef — since on its own it is permitted [to carry within it], now too it is permitted, and they do not prohibit one another; for had there been a partition between them, it would have been permitted to carry from this [one] to that [one] according to Rabbi Shimon, and now that they are breached into one another, they have not breached into a domain that is forbidden to it. But [if the sown area is] more than two beit se'a, it becomes a karmelit, and in this [case] even Rabbi Shimon concedes that one may not carry from a courtyard into a karpef of more than two beit se'a that was not enclosed for dwelling purposes; and here, since they are breached into one another, behold, each one is breached into a place that is forbidden to it.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:5:1.hebrew: איצטבלאות - נטועין שורות שורות, ונאה לשבת שם:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:5:1.english: In rows [itztablaot] - [They are] planted row by row, and it is pleasant to sit there.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:6:1.hebrew: לבי רב הונא - ויותר מבית סאתים הוה, והוקף לדירה, וניטע אחרי כן:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:6:1.english: To the house of Rav Huna - And it was more than a beit se'atayim, and was enclosed for [the purpose of] dwelling, and planted afterward.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:7:1.hebrew: קרפף יותר מבית סאתים שלא הוקף לדירה - ואחרי כן בנה אצלו דירה, ואמרי' לקמן: הוקף שלא לדירה ולבסוף פתח לו פתח דירת ביתו — לא מהני:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:7:1.english: A karpef greater than two beit se’a that was not enclosed for residence - And afterward he built a residence next to it. And we say later: [If an area] was enclosed not for [the purpose of] residence, and ultimately he opened into it an entrance [from] the residence of his house, it is not effective.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:7:2.hebrew: כיצד הוא עושה פורץ לו פרצה יותר מעשר - דהוי כמי שאין בו מחיצות, וגודר וסותם אותה פירצה ומעמידה על עשר, והוי כפתח, ולבסוף הוקף לדירה שנפתחה לו. דלעולם בעינן שיגדור יותר מעשר אמות, דאי פריץ עשר לבד וגדרה, לא חשיב ההוא היקף לשם דירה, אלא כמי שעשה פתח, דעד עשר לעולם הוי פתח:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:7:2.english: What should one do? He should make a breach in it larger than ten - For [by doing so] it becomes as though it has no partitions; and he fences and closes up that breach and leaves it standing at ten [cubits], and it is [then considered] an entrance, and [thus] ultimately it was enclosed for the sake of the dwelling that was opened into it. For we always require that he fence [part of a breach of] more than ten cubits, because if he breached only ten [cubits] and fenced it, that enclosure is not considered [an enclosure] for the purpose of a dwelling, but rather like someone who made an entrance, for up to ten [cubits] is always [considered] an entrance.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:8:1.hebrew: פרץ אמה - אצל סתימה וגדרה, ועוד פרץ אמה אצל סתימת אמה החדשה וגדרה — דלא פרץ י' אמות כאחד, ולא גדר עשר אמות בבת אחת, אלא מעט היה פורץ וגודר מיד:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:8:1.english: He breached a cubit - Adjacent to a closed [section of the wall] and fenced it, and further breached a cubit adjacent to the closed [section of] the new cubit and fenced it — so that he did not breach ten cubits at once and did not fence ten cubits at one time, but rather he would breach a little and fence [it] immediately.

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:8:2.hebrew: עד שהשלימו ליותר מעשר - מי אמרינן: כיון דלא פרץ י' בבת אחת ולא גדר בבת אחת, לא הויא היקף בזו לשם דירה? או דילמא: כיון דהשתא מיהא הוי החידוש של היקף יותר מעשר, חשיב היקף לשם דירה:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:8:2.english: Until he completed it to more than ten [cubits] - Do we say: Since he did not breach ten [cubits] at once and did not fence [them] at once, in this [case] it does not become an enclosure for the purpose of dwelling? Or perhaps: Since now, at any rate, the renewal of the enclosure is more than ten [cubits], it is considered an enclosure for the purpose of dwelling?

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:9:1.english: All utensils belonging to homeowners - With regard to wooden utensils, we learned this in Tractate Kelim (17:1).

Rashi on Eruvin 24a:9:2.hebrew: שיעורן כרמונים - לטהר מטומאתן, אבל פחות מכאן — חייס עליה ולא מבטיל ליה. שיעורן כרמונים: ניקב כמוציא רמון — טהור:
Rashi on Eruvin 24a:9:2.english: Their measure is like pomegranates - [This is the measure required] to purify them from their [ritual] impurity; but [for a hole] less than this, he spares [the vessel] and does not nullify it [from use as a utensil]. “Their measure is like pomegranates” — [meaning that if] it was perforated [with a hole large enough] for a pomegranate to emerge, it is pure.

Tosafot on Eruvin 24a:11:1.hebrew: סנדל שנפסקה וכו' - הוא הדין בלא תקנה נמי דטמא מדרס; דאי כשנפסקה פרחה לה טומאה — תו לא הדרה לה, דלא מצינו טומאה ישנה חוזרת אלא בכלי מתכות, כדמפרש בסוף פ"ק דשבת (ד' טז.). והא דנקט "ותקנה", פ"ה: לאשמועינן, אע"ג דתקנה — כי נפסקה שניה, טהורה מן המדרס, דפנים חדשות באו לכאן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 24a:11:1.english: "A sandal that [one of its straps] broke, etc." - The same ruling applies even without repairing it, that it is [still] impure with midras [impurity]; for if the impurity had departed when it broke, it would not return to it [upon repair], since we do not find that old impurity returns except in the case of metal vessels, as [the Gemara] explains at the end of the first chapter of Shabbat (16a). And as for that which [the tanna] stated, "and he repaired it," the Kuntres [Rashi] explained: [It is] to teach us that even though he repaired it, when the second [strap] broke, it is pure from midras [impurity], for a new entity has arrived here.

Tosafot on Eruvin 24a:12:1.hebrew: אבל טמא מגע מדרס - פירש הקונטרס: משום דעדיין כלי הוא לאישתמושי ביה תשמישתא אחרינא. ולפירושו, אפילו נפסקה שניה טמא מגע מדרס. וקשה, דתנן בהדיא בסיפא דהך משנה במסכת כלים בפרק כ"ו (מ"ד): "לא הספיק לתקן ראשונה עד שנפסקה שניה — טהורה". ורש"י חזר בו והגיה: "אבל טמא מגע מדרס — דעדיין כלי הוא וחזי למילתא קמייתא, דהא איתקנה ראשונה". ולפירושו, איצטריך למיתני ברישא "ותיקנה", דאי לא נתקנה, כי נפסקה שניה אינה טמאה אפילו מגע מדרס; ואגב דתני ברישא, תני נמי בסיפא. ומיהו תימה: מתי בא לו מגע מדרס? דאם בא לו מגע מדרס ומדרס יחד — כגון שדרס עליו הזב ברגלו יחף, או אפי' במנעל ולא הפסיק בפשוטי כלי עץ — א"כ איכא פנים חדשות למגע מדרס כמו למדרס! ולפי' רש"י קמא ניחא, דאפילו נפסקו ב' אזנים טמא מגע מדרס, הואיל וחזי לתשמיש אחרינא. ובפרק אלו קשרים (שבת דף קיב:) פ"ה דטמא מגע מדרס לפי שנגע בעצמו כשהיה אב הטומאה. ולא נהירא, דטומאת בית הסתרים היא, דלא קיימא לן כרבי מאיר דאמר מטמא, מדפריך בפשיטות בפרק בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עב:) ובהעור והרוטב (שם דף קכט:): "טומאת בית הסתרים היא". ומה שפירש כאן נמי, דבשעת פרישתו מאוזן קיבל טומאה מאביו — אינו נראה, דבפרק בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עב:) אמרינן דבעינן באות מבגד גדול. ואין לומר דכשתיקן אוזן ראשון, לאחר שתפר חציה נעשית מחוברת ובא לה טומאת מדרס שבטלה לסנדל, וכשחזר ותפר חציה השניה בא לסנדל מגע מדרס מן האוזן, ותו ליכא פנים חדשות — דא"כ תפשוט בעיין דהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף כד.) דלא אמרינן שבע לה טומאה! ולהר"ר שמעון מיינבי"א דמפרש דלא אמרינן שבע לה טומאה היכא דטומאה בא לו מגופו, אתי שפיר. ועוד יש לומר, דלאוזן בא מגע מדרס ומדרס יחד כשתפרה לסנדל, והסנדל בטל לאוזן, דאי אפשר להיות טומאה לזה בלא זה; וכיון שבאו לה כאחד, אין שייך לומר גביה שבע לה טומאה. וריצב"א אומר דלא שייך גבי מגע פנים חדשות, דאפילו נפסקו שתי אזניו ראוי לקבל טומאת מגע אם מיחדו לתשמיש אחר, ולא נתבטל תורת יחוד מכאן, דכל שעה ושעה מתקנו ודעתו להשתמש בו; אבל לנועלו, אם נפסקו שתי אזניו, אפילו מיחדו — בטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם:
Tosafot on Eruvin 24a:12:1.english: "However, it is impure with contact of midras" - Rashi explained: Because it is still a vessel to be used for another purpose. But according to his explanation, even if the second [ear] broke, it would be impure with contact of midras! And this is difficult, for it is taught explicitly in the latter clause of this Mishnah in tractate Kelim, chapter 26 (Mishnah 4): "If he did not manage to repair the first before the second broke, it is pure." And Rashi retracted and emended [his commentary]: "'However, it is impure with contact of midras' — for it is still a vessel and fit for its original purpose, since the first [ear] was repaired." And according to his explanation, it was necessary to teach in the first clause "and he repaired it," for had it not been repaired, when the second broke it would not be impure even with contact of midras; and since it taught [this phrasing] in the first clause, it also taught [it] in the latter clause. However, it is astonishing: When did contact of midras come to it? For if contact of midras and midras came to it together — such as where the zav stepped on it with his bare foot, or even with a shoe and did not interpose with flat wooden vessels — if so, there are "new faces" with respect to contact of midras just as with respect to midras! And according to Rashi's first explanation this is well, for even if both ears broke, it is impure with contact of midras since it is fit for another purpose. And in the chapter [entitled] Elu Ksharim (Shabbat 112b), Rashi explained that it is impure with contact of midras because it touched itself when it was a primary source of impurity. But this does not seem correct, for it is impurity in a concealed part, and we do not hold in accordance with Rabbi Meir who says it transmits impurity, since the Gemara asks simply in the chapter [entitled] Behemah Hamaksheh (Chullin 72b) and in [the chapter entitled] Ha'or Veharotev (ibid. 129b): "Is it not impurity in a concealed part?" And that which he explained here as well, that at the time of its separation from the ear it received impurity from its "father" [the primary source of impurity], does not seem correct, for in the chapter [entitled] Behemah Hamaksheh (Chullin 72b) we say that we require [remnants] coming from a large garment. And one cannot say that when he repaired the first ear, after he had sewn half of it, it became attached and midras impurity came to it as it became subordinate to the sandal, and when he then went back and sewed its second half, contact of midras came to the sandal from the ear, and therefore there are no longer "new faces" — for if so, you would resolve our dilemma in [the chapter entitled] Hakometz Rabbah (Menachot 24a) [and prove] that we do not say "it is sated with impurity"! And according to the Rabbi, R. Shimon of Joinville, who explains that we do not say "it is sated with impurity" where the impurity comes to it from its own body, it works out well. And furthermore, one can say that to the ear came contact of midras and midras together when he sewed it to the sandal, and the sandal was subordinate to the ear, for it is impossible for there to be impurity for one without the other; and since they came to it at once, it is not applicable to say regarding it "it is sated with impurity." And the Ritzba says that "new faces" is not applicable regarding contact [impurity], for even if both of its ears broke, it is fit to receive contact impurity if he designates it for another use, and the status of designation was not nullified here, since at every single moment he repairs it and his intention is to use it. But for wearing it, if both of its ears broke, even if he designates it, his intention is nullified by that of all people.

Tosafot on Eruvin 24a:18:1.hebrew: פשיטא לא צריכא דאית ביה בי דרי - אדרב נחמן, דאמר: "אם פתח בו פתח מותר לטלטל", פריך — דמפרש הש"ס: בפתח ולבסוף הוקף, ואהא פריך: "פשיטא!" אבל אש"ס דמפרש "לא אמרן", לא פריך — דקמ"ל: הוקף ולבסוף פתח לא מהני, לאפוקי מהני אמוראי דלקמן (עירובין ד' כה:) גבי אבורנקי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 24a:18:1.english: "It is obvious! It is necessary only where there is a threshing floor" - [The Gemara] poses its challenge against Rav Naḥman, who said: "If one opened an entrance to it, it is permitted to carry [throughout the entire area]," for the Gemara explains [his statement as referring to a case] where he opened [the entrance] and afterward fenced [it] in, and on this [the Gemara] challenges: "It is obvious!" But against the Gemara [itself], which explains "We stated [this] only [where he opened and afterward fenced it in]," [the Gemara] does not pose a challenge, for it teaches us that [if] it was fenced in and afterward he opened [an entrance], it is not effective, to exclude [the opinion of] those Amora'im below (Eruvin 25b) regarding the pavilion [avurnaqi].

Tosafot on Eruvin 24a:2:1.hebrew: לא אמרן אלא דלא הוי בית סאתים - אע"ג דלרבנן קרפף פחות מבית סאתים דינו כקרפף בית סאתים לטלטל ממנו לחצר, משום דאין סברא שיהו שלשה חילוקים בשלשה משהויין — הכא לא אסר מיעוט הנזרע לרוב שאינו נזרע במה שפרוץ לו במלואו; דכיון שהוא פחות מבית סאתים, לא חשיב, ובטל לגבי רוב שאינו נזרע. אבל בית סאתים חשיב טפי, ולא בטיל. ובנזרע רובו — אפי' לא הוי בית סאתים אסור, דבטיל לגבי רובו, והוה כנזרע כולו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 24a:2:1.english: We said [that it is permitted] only if [the sown section] is not [as large as] two beit se’a - Even though according to the Rabbis, a karpef of less than two beit se’a has the same law as a karpef of two beit se’a regarding carrying from it into a courtyard — because it does not stand to reason that there should be three distinctions within three minimal increments — here, the sown minority does not prohibit the unsown majority by virtue of being fully open to it; for since it is less than two beit se’a, it is not significant, and it is nullified relative to the unsown majority. But [if the sown section is] two beit se’a, it is more significant and is not nullified. And if the majority of it was sown, even if [the sown area] is not two beit se’a, it is prohibited, because [the unsown minority] is nullified relative to the majority of it, and it is as though the entirety of it were sown.
